proof.text: Let $H$ be any acyclic complex of $R$-module sheaves. Since $P$ is K-flat, $\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)$ is acyclic by the defining test for K-flatness. Applying K-flatness of $Q$ to this acyclic complex gives that $\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)\otimes_R Q)$ is acyclic. The direct-sum total differential identifies this complex with $\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R T)$ by the reassociation map described below. Thus $T$ is K-flat. The argument quantifies over all acyclic $H$ and uses no boundedness in either direction.

For every pair of degrees $p,q$, the sheaf $P^p\otimes_R Q^q$ is flat: for an $R$-module sheaf $G$, the associativity isomorphism of the symmetric monoidal structure of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] gives $G\otimes_R(P^p\otimes_R Q^q)\cong(G\otimes_R P^p)\otimes_R Q^q$ naturally in $G$, so tensoring on the right by $P^p\otimes_RQ^q$ is isomorphic to the composite of tensoring on the right by $P^p$ and then by $Q^q$; both functors are exact because the corresponding terms are flat, and a composite of exact functors is exact. This works for arbitrary integers $p,q$.

For fixed $i$, the index set of pairs $(p,q)$ with $p+q=i$ is countable. Therefore $T^i=\bigoplus_{p+q=i}P^p\otimes_R Q^q$ is a countable direct sum of flat sheaves, hence flat by the countable-direct-sum clause of [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. This proves flatness of every term of $T$, including for unbounded $P$ and $Q$.

proof.text: On the summand indexed by integers $(a,p,q)$ with $a+p+q=n$, define $h\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(h\otimes x)\otimes y$, the associativity isomorphism $H^a\otimes_R(P^p\otimes_RQ^q)\cong(H^a\otimes_RP^p)\otimes_RQ^q$ of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. By the same node, $H^a\otimes_R-$ is a left adjoint and so commutes with arbitrary direct sums, and by symmetry so does $-\otimes_RQ^q$; hence the degree-$n$ term of each side is $\bigoplus_{a+p+q=n}H^a\otimes_RP^p\otimes_RQ^q$ (bracketed accordingly), and taking the direct sum of the summand maps over all such triples gives a degreewise isomorphism $\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R T)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)\otimes_R Q)$. The differential on the source has the three components $dh\otimes(x\otimes y)$, $(-1)^a h\otimes(dx\otimes y)$, $(-1)^{a+p}h\otimes(x\otimes dy)$ with signs $1,(-1)^a,(-1)^{a+p}$, and the reassociated target has $(dh\otimes x)\otimes y$, $(-1)^a(h\otimes dx)\otimes y$, $(-1)^{a+p}(h\otimes x)\otimes dy$ with the same three signs; since the associativity isomorphism is natural, the map commutes with the differential. Its inverse is the inverse reassociation on each summand, and naturality in $H$ follows from naturality of the associator. Direct sums make this valid without boundedness assumptions.

proof.text: The complex $T$ is K-flat with flat terms by Steps 1 and 3, so $T$ lies in the resolving subcategory $\mathcal P_R$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Applying its canonical model comparison to $P,Q\in\mathcal P_R$ gives $Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)\cong Q_RP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_RQ$. Since $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$, this is the claimed identification of the localized object of $T$ with the derived tensor of the localized objects. title: K-flat total tensor model for flat-term resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $P,Q$ be possibly unbounded, integer-indexed cochain complexes of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], both K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and with flat terms [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Their direct-sum total tensor $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ is K-flat and has flat terms, including when both complexes are unbounded in both directions. Explicitly, each term $T^i=\bigoplus_{p+q=i}P^p\otimes_R Q^q$ is flat. For every complex $H$ there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R T)\cong\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)\otimes_R Q),$$
whose restriction to degree $(a,p,q)$ is $h\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(h\otimes x)\otimes y$, with the direct-sum total differentials. The localized object of $T$ is the derived tensor of the localized objects of $P,Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; hence $T$ is itself a flat-term K-flat representative that can be used in a further derived tensor or derived pullback. No boundedness or flatness of the cohomology sheaves is assumed.
